task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about public access planned for the club-leased ballfield in Coppermead. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Coppermead Athletics Club's exclusive lease of the city-owned Mill Acre ballfield ends Sept. 30, 2026, without renewal.
The city has owned the 11-acre property throughout the 30-year lease, so the change does not involve buying the land from the club.
The parks department plans to open the ground for general recreation in April 2027 after access and drainage work.
The fence will remain closed during the work, and the end of the lease does not immediately open the field to the public.
The council approved a $275,000 works allowance, but final contractor prices have not yet been obtained.
The initial work includes a step-free entrance, repairs to the perimeter path and improvements to the wet corner nearest the pavilion.
Under a new booking agreement, the club will retain 12 scheduled training hours a week without retaining exclusive control of the property.
Other organized groups will use the city's booking system, while casual use will be possible outside reserved sessions.
Parks director Soren Vale said, "Opening a gate is simple; making room for different uses is the work that comes after it."
The club has agreed to transfer ownership of the small equipment shed to the city while removing its privately owned training equipment.
Club secretary Mara Keel said, "We lose the certainty of having the whole place, but we keep a place to train."
Nearby residents have asked for seating and informal play space rather than turning every available hour into another organized booking.
The current plan does not add floodlights or authorize late-night events at the field.
Proposed public opening hours are 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.; the council will confirm them with the final management plan.
A dog-access policy has not been settled and will be considered alongside maintenance and sports-use requirements.
The city will take over routine grounds maintenance, which is currently the club's responsibility under its lease.
The operating budget for that maintenance will be considered separately from the capital works allowance.
The pavilion toilets will remain closed until their condition assessment and repair scope are complete.
The club's noticeboard displays handwritten match results dating to its first season on the ground.
The local history society has offered to photograph the noticeboard before the pavilion is altered.
No attendance forecast or estimate of additional local business spending accompanies the approved transition plan.
The parks department will publish a works timetable after procurement and hold a management-plan meeting before public opening.

forbidden_additions: A land purchase from the club or immediate unrestricted opening.
Loss of all club training access, approved floodlights or a settled dog policy.
Guaranteed April completion, fully funded ongoing maintenance or attendance forecasts.
preserve: The change from exclusive leasing to shared public and booked use.
Separate capital work, operating costs and unresolved management decisions.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
